subject: System Design
title: Consistency vs Availability
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Consistency vs Availability.

hook.text: You post a photo. Your friend in Tokyo doesn't see it for 10 seconds. Is that a bug?

buildup.text: Consistency means everyone sees the same data at the same time. Availability means the system always responds.

discovery.text: The CAP theorem says during a network partition, you must choose consistency or availability — not both.

twist.text: Banks choose consistency — your balance must be correct. Social media chooses availability — a slight delay is fine.

climax.text: There's no universal answer. The right choice depends on what your users can tolerate.

punchline.text: Correct or always-on — pick one during failures.

quiz.question: What does the CAP theorem state?
options: During a partition, you must choose consistency or availability
All three guarantees are always possible
